trial_court: Family Court, Angul, Case No.63 of 2021
case_name: Kedarnath Panda vs Ritika Nanda — TRP (C) No.426 of 2021
facts_of_case: Petitioner-husband initiated CP No.143 of 2021 under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act in Bhubaneswar court, but opp. party filed TRP (C) No.102 of 2021 for transfer to Angul. Court declined transfer and directed certain actions. Petitioner now seeks transfer to Bhubaneswar due to professional and educational commitments.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking transfer to show that it is necessary and justifiable.
legal_principles.held: He further submits that the petitioner is a doctor by profession and is presently pursuing his Post Graduation course at M.K.C.G. Medical College and Hospital, Berhampur by taking the study loan and he is staying with his aged parents in Bhubaneswar in a flat for which he and his father have taken home loan.
cited_cases: Kedarnath Panda vs Ritika Nanda, (2022) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: Convenience and expediency are relevant considerations in determining the transfer of a case.
legal_principles.held: On the other hand, if the case is transferred to Bhubaneswar which is closer to Berhampur, it will be convenient for both parties as the parents of the opp. party are also residing in Bhubaneswar.
cited_cases: Kedarnath Panda vs Ritika Nanda, (2022) X SCC Y

outcome.final_order: Case transferred to Family Court, Bhubaneswar.

use_for_drafting: advising on transfer of cases between courts
